# Verification analysis: firewall-log-correlation-rhel9

Job: `2026-09-06__00-21-44`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Traffic from `node3` to `node4` on TCP port 23 crosses `node1` first and
> `node2` second. Have `node1` permit that traffic and record it, and `node2`
> refuse it and record the refusal, then show the pair of log entries produced
> by one attempt from `node3` so the point where the traffic stopped is
> evident from the records alone.

## Environment

- Systems: **1 vyos + 1 opnsense + 2 rhel9.8**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `firewall-log-correlation-rhel9__jZGSGHV`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct, correlated log evidence: node1 permits and logs the tcp/23 flow, node2 rejects and logs the same flow, and a single-attempt correlated pair of log entries (matching IP ID and source port) unambiguously shows the traffic passing node1 and stopping at node2 — demonstrated both before and after a full restart of all four nodes. The independent restart-evidence protocol was executed thoroughly on all four nodes with clear boot-identity transitions and post-restart functional verification. Hygiene is generally good with only minor residue (unremoved temp scripts/backup on node2, a possibly orphaned backgrounded monitor process on node1) and a post-restart failed systemd unit on the two RHEL nodes that was not investigated.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.720 | 0.900 | 49/6 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **node1-permit-log — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS) permits the node3->node4 TCP/23 traffic and records (logs) it
  - **Why:** VyOS forward-filter rule 10 (protocol tcp, dest 10.100.40.13/23, action accept, log enabled) was committed and saved (cmd-e43218bef58b4670), confirmed present after the initial attempt (cmd-245a10069ead4f9d, kernel log '[ipv4-FWD-filter-10-A] ...ACCEPT') and again after a full reboot cycle on a fresh attempt (cmd-b726de83d4434097, matching IP ID/source port). Traffic is clearly permitted and logged at node1 on two separate attempts.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e43218bef58b4670`, `cmd-245a10069ead4f9d`, `cmd-b726de83d4434097`, `cmd-eda958ed7ed844b1`
- **node2-refuse-log — Satisfied:** node2 (OPNsense) refuses the same traffic and records the refusal
  - **Why:** A reject+log filter rule for tcp/23 to 10.100.40.13 was inserted ahead of default-allow rules and applied via configctl filter reload (cmd-2ad5b3d303cc44aa, cmd-76af8260d4f44a6c). pf filterlog captured a 'block' entry for the flow on the first attempt (cmd-53b06a7ed5214c71) and again on a fresh attempt after a full reboot (cmd-e69a63b8de8643e2). node3's own connection attempts returned 'Connection refused' (cmd-e83510a596b048a7, cmd-0a290f40836d4f9b), consistent with the reject action.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2ad5b3d303cc44aa`, `cmd-76af8260d4f44a6c`, `cmd-53b06a7ed5214c71`, `cmd-e69a63b8de8643e2`

  - **Why:** In the post-restart demonstration attempt (cmd-0a290f40836d4f9b), node1's kernel log shows an ACCEPT entry with IP ID=1116, SPT=51802 for the SYN packet (cmd-b726de83d4434097), and node2's pf filterlog shows a 'block' entry for the identical packet (same IP ID=1116 and source port=51802) at the same timestamp (cmd-e69a63b8de8643e2). The matching identifiers make it clear from the two records alone that the packet passed node1 and was stopped at node2. ### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.720**. Most executor mutations were purposeful and either persisted as intended (firewall rules, static routes) or were bounded, ephemeral test aids (host route, socat listener) reasonably re-created after reboot. A few minor issues: (1) trial-and-error VyOS 'log enable'/'log ?' set attempts (cmd-a66a5188905441dc, cmd-0ff1e0146dbd4195) failed harmlessly and were corrected by the working 'set ... log' command, not a lasting mutation. (2) On node2 the executor left temp scripts and a config backup (/tmp/config.xml.bak, /tmp/addrule.py, /tmp/fixlog.py from cmd-2ad5b3d303cc44aa and cmd-76af8260d4f44a6c) with no observed cleanup; low risk but unremoved residue. (3) node1's 'run monitor firewall' was launched as a backgrounded shell job (cmd-df1031e8d34541f9) with no confirmed termination, a minor orphaned-process risk. (4) The after-executor lifecycle snapshot shows a newly-failed systemd unit (NetworkManager-wait-online.service) on both node3 and node4 that was not present at baseline; this appears to be a side effect of the native reboot used for the restart-evidence protocol rather than of the firewall configuration itself, and was not investigated or remediated by the executor.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-a66a5188905441dc`, `cmd-0ff1e0146dbd4195`, `cmd-2ad5b3d303cc44aa`, `cmd-76af8260d4f44a6c`, `cmd-df1031e8d34541f9`, `global:after_executor:node3:failed-services`, `global:after_executor:node4:failed-services`, `global:before_prepare:node3:failed-services`, `global:before_prepare:node4:failed-services`

### Comments and limitations

- The 'run monitor firewall' background job on node1 (cmd-df1031e8d34541f9) was never explicitly confirmed terminated; its continued state is unknown.
- Temp files /tmp/config.xml.bak, /tmp/addrule.py, /tmp/fixlog.py created on node2 were not observed to be cleaned up.
- NetworkManager-wait-online.service is shown failed on node3 and node4 only after the executor's restart cycle; the trace does not establish whether this is transient/benign or a persistent degradation, since no follow-up check was performed.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.720); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
